summary: ING sits at 0.407 on the traditional-to-challenger axis — still recognisably traditional, but leaning towards the challengers. Its largest measured deviations from peers are not about clarity but about pressure: urgency and deadline language (4.0 against a peer mean of 0.64) and persuasion techniques used (5.0 against 1.67), while clarity of the offer (5.0 against 3.97), mobile-first design (1.0 against 0.56) and making the offer feel worth having (1.0 against 0.59) are strengths. No performance data exists in this project, so every recommendation below is a hypothesis to test, and cross-bank comparisons remain confounded by product family and page language.

recommendations.title: Cut deadline and urgency language
recommendations.finding: ING uses urgency and deadline language 4.0 times per page on average, against a peer mean of 0.64 — a gap of 3.69 standard deviations and one of the two strongest deviations in ING's whole profile.
recommendations.recommendation: Remove countdowns, "last days" and deadline wording from the current-account pages; where an offer genuinely ends, state the end date once in plain text instead of repeating the time pressure across hero, body and call to action.

recommendations.title: Stop stacking persuasion techniques
recommendations.finding: ING averages 5.0 persuasion techniques per page against a peer mean of 1.67 (gap 3.68 standard deviations), the second-largest deviation measured for ING.
recommendations.recommendation: Choose one persuasion technique per page — for example a single reason to switch — and delete the other stacked appeals from the same hero and body blocks, so the page argues once rather than five times.

recommendations.title: Put the conditions next to the "free" claim
recommendations.finding: "Free" appears with conditions attached on 0.67 of ING pages against a peer mean of 0.23 (gap 1.03 standard deviations), and legal small print is carried by 0.93 of traditional pages against 0.5 of challenger pages.
recommendations.recommendation: Wherever an account is described as free, place the qualifying condition in the same visual block as the word "free" and repeat it in the call to action, rather than leaving it to the small print at the foot of the page.

recommendations.title: Shorten the campaign pages
recommendations.finding: ING pages run to about 11,149 px against a peer mean of about 6,412 px (gap 1.42 standard deviations). Read the measurement as exact about geometry and approximate about meaning.
recommendations.recommendation: Cut each page back towards peer length by removing repeated product blocks, stacked FAQ sections and duplicate image sections — not by deleting the offer statement itself.

recommendations.title: Consolidate images into fewer, larger visuals
recommendations.finding: ING shows 33 images per page against a peer mean of 19 (gap 0.85 standard deviations). Across the market, challengers give imagery a larger share of the page (0.31 against 0.1 for traditional banks) and a larger opening image (0.62 against 0.25), so the difference is in how imagery is broken up rather than how much of it there is.
recommendations.recommendation: Replace clusters of small repeated images with one stronger opening visual and a few supporting ones, keeping the existing mobile-first layout intact.

recommendations.title: Make the fast sign-up promise concrete
recommendations.finding: ING promises fast digital sign-up on 0.67 of its pages against a peer mean of 0.15 (gap 1.42 standard deviations), but the claim is not linked to any outcome, because no performance data exists in this project.
recommendations.recommendation: Under the sign-up promise, spell out in a short visible sequence what the customer does and what happens next, and route the main call to action to the start of that sequence instead of leaving the promise as a headline assertion.

recommendations.title: Test a less bright opening treatment
recommendations.finding: ING's page brightness measures 0.55 against a peer mean of 0.34 (gap 1.4 standard deviations), and brightness is also what separates traditional from challenger pages in this dataset (0.43 against 0.17). Brightness was captured in a single rendering, so read this as a comparison of our captures only.
recommendations.recommendation: Test a darker, image-led hero against the current bright hero on one page and keep whichever version holds attention, rather than changing the palette across the site.

recommendations.title: Protect the plain offer statement while rewriting
recommendations.finding: Clarity of the offer (5.0 against a peer mean of 3.97), mobile-first design (1.0 against 0.56) and making the offer feel worth having (1.0 against 0.59) are all above the peer mean — these are the strengths that should survive the cuts to length and urgency.
recommendations.recommendation: Anchor every rewritten page on one plain-language offer statement above the fold, and check the first screen on a phone before publishing, so the shortening work does not remove the clarity that currently beats peers.

recommendations.title: Match digital claims to what the press is actually covering
recommendations.finding: ING's 90-day news themes contain no innovation or digital items — its two headlines sit under the theme "other" (analyst coverage and a shared piece on daily transfer limits) — while the pages put a fast digital sign-up promise in front of the customer more often than peers do. The link between the two is a hypothesis to verify, not evidence about page performance.
recommendations.recommendation: On pages that promise fast digital sign-up, replace leadership-style digital framing with a concrete, checkable description of the sign-up steps and where to get help, and test whether that version reads more credibly.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING has 2 headlines in the 90-day window, both counted under the theme "other" (notable headlines include "ING op de favorietenlijst van JPMorgan" and "ING, Belfius, BNP, Crelan... Vos virements limités à 5.000 € par jour, mais est-ce le cas dans toutes les banques ?"); no headline is themed innovation_digital.

recommendations.title: Keep urgency framing away from payment and security copy
recommendations.finding: One of ING's two headlines in the window is a shared article about daily transfer limits and the other is analyst coverage; both are counted under the theme "other", and nothing in the window is a campaign or promotion theme. Whether heavy deadline framing on account-opening pages sits awkwardly next to payments and limits coverage is a hypothesis to verify, not a measured effect.
recommendations.recommendation: On account-opening and current-account pages, keep deadline and countdown wording out of any section that talks about payments, transfer limits or security, and state those limits plainly in that section instead.
recommendations.reputation_context: Two ING headlines in the last 90 days, both under the theme "other"; one is a shared article on daily transfer limits at several Belgian banks.
